samples.summary: The chip's new "turn on offline saving" offer ignores `useDurabilityPermitted()`, so it is shown on the share-link route that `NonDurableScope` explicitly marks as never-durable.
samples.evidence: `offerOffline = stranded && supportsClientKey() && !offlineEnabled` (sync-status-chip.tsx:86) consults the capability gate and the preference, but not the positional permission the same change introduced. The reaching site is out of the diff: `packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-header-status.tsx:26` renders `<SyncStatusChip />`, and `shared-document.tsx:317/393/443/526/652` mount `SharedHeaderStatus` inside `CollabDocumentProvider`, which the diff wraps in `NonDurableScope` (shared-document.tsx:1007). So a share-link `editor` who goes offline gets the chip rendered as a clickable `<button>` plus a toast action offering to enable device saving — on a document the new guard guarantees will never be persisted. `useDurabilityPermitted` is already exported from `@/lib/use-durable-document` for exactly this kind of caller and is read two files away in `collab-document-provider.tsx`. Nothing is persisted (the scope still blocks it), so this is a misleading surface rather than a data leak; the fix belongs on the new `offerOffline` expression.

samples.summary: `OfflineRuntime` is mounted for every authenticated session with no capability or preference gate, so all users pay an extra `GET /documents`, an IndexedDB database creation and localStorage writes for a feature that is dark on this build.
samples.evidence: `PrivateRoute.tsx:35` renders `<OfflineRuntime userId={String(me.id)} />` unconditionally. `offline-runtime.tsx:62-150` then runs, on every mount, `rememberOfflineUser` (writes `wafflebase-offline-user`), `new WafflebaseDocStore({userId})`, `retryPendingOfflineErase()`, `store.collectStale()` (opens/creates the `wafflebase-offline` database) and `await fetchDocuments()` followed by `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments`. Nothing in that effect consults `supportsClientKey()` or `getOfflinePersistenceEnabled()` — unlike every other surface, which the diff deliberately gates (settings/page.tsx:111, sync-status-chip.tsx:86, use-durable-document.ts `eligibleNow`). `packages/frontend/package.json:66` pins `@yorkie-js/react` at `0.7.22`, below `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"` (yorkie-capabilities.ts), so `supportsClientKey()` is false and nothing can ever be stored on this build — yet every signed-in page load still issues a full unpaginated document listing to `GET /documents` (document.controller.ts:180) and creates an IndexedDB database on the user's disk. Also note `logout()` (api/auth.ts:116) now unconditionally opens that database for every user because `rememberOfflineUser` populated the identity. Nothing breaks; the cost is fleet-wide request volume and a surprise database for users who never opted in.

samples.summary: A file in the production source tree (`src/lib/`) top-level-imports `vitest`, placing a devDependency import on the app's module graph.
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/lib/doc-store-contract.ts:1` is `import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest";` in a non-`.test.ts` file under `src/lib/`. Today its only importer is `packages/frontend/src/lib/wafflebase-doc-store.test.ts:4`, so nothing breaks. But every other module under `src/lib/` is production code, and the frontend has no `tsc` lane, so a future import of this module from a real path would pull `vitest` into the bundle (or fail the `vite build` resolve) with nothing in CI pointing at the cause. Convention elsewhere in this package is that shared test helpers live beside their suites or under `tests/` — e.g. `packages/frontend/tests/setup.ts`. Moving it out of `src/lib/` (or renaming it so the test globs own it) removes the hazard.
